summary:
MEDULA is an offline-first health intelligence platform designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. Addressing the five hazards of human spaceflight identified by NASA, MEDULA brings together physiological measurements, manual health assessments, sleep and activity records, and radiation exposure data.
The system establishes personalised health baselines, detects unusual changes across multiple health indicators, and connects these observations with mission activities and environmental context. It provides explainable health insights, follow-up assessment guidance, and access to relevant research resources, including NASA's Spaceflight Standard Measures.
With local data storage and offline capabilities, MEDULA is designed to remain useful when communication with Earth is limited. By moving beyond isolated measurements towards personalised, context-aware health assessment, MEDULA aims to help astronauts better understand their health and make informed decisions throughout their missions.
details:
MEDULA

MEDULA (Autonomous Astronaut Health Intelligence System) is an offline-first platform designed to support astronaut health assessment during long-duration space missions.

How It Works

MEDULA collects health information through four primary sources: wearable physiological measurements, manual health assessments, mission activity records and radiation dosimeter readings.

The system processes this information through interconnected intelligence modules:

  1. Data Acquisition and Validation: Collects health records, validates measurements and preserves data quality and provenance.
  2. Personal Baseline Engine: Establishes individual health baselines using historical measurements and statistical methods such as mean, median and standard deviation.
  3. Multi-Indicator Pattern Detection: Identifies unusual changes and combinations of health indicators over time.
  4. Mission Context Engine: Examines relevant sleep, exercise, workload and environmental information alongside health observations.
  5. Medical Decision Support: Explains detected findings and provides appropriate follow-up assessment guidance using relevant research and configured medical protocols.
  6. Mission Continuity: Supports local data storage, offline access and synchronisation when connectivity becomes available.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MEDULA moves beyond monitoring isolated health measurements by considering individual health history and mission context. It aims to help astronauts recognise meaningful health changes, understand contributing observations and make informed decisions when communication with Earth is limited.

Its offline-first approach supports continued access to locally stored health information during communication interruptions.

Technology Used

  • Frontend: React.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js.
  • Database: MongoDB and IndexedDB using Dexie.js.
  • Data Validation: Zod.
  • Visualisation: Recharts.
  • Application Architecture: Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline capabilities.
  • Development Environment: Google Antigravity, VS Code and GitHub.

The prototype is designed to accept measurements from compatible wearable devices and radiation dosimeters, alongside manual astronaut inputs.

Creativity and Innovation

MEDULA's main innovation is personalised, multi-indicator health pattern detection. Instead of relying on universal health values or isolated alerts, it compares measurements against individual baselines and examines how multiple indicators change together.

It also connects health observations with mission activities, making its explanations more meaningful and context-aware.

Design Considerations

The project considers NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields and hostile closed environments.

We also prioritised offline availability, data integrity, individual health differences, explainability, usability and scientific responsibility. NASA's Spaceflight Standard Measures serves as a research reference for selecting relevant health indicators.

MEDULA is a research prototype intended to support astronaut self-assessment. It does not replace professional medical judgement or certified onboard medical protocols.
